description: The bar chart illustrates the average number of tokens used in reasoning and demonstration components across different numbers of shots (0, 1, 2, 3, and 4) in a few-shot prompting setup, as described in the paper "Mapping the Minds of LLMs: A Graph-Based Analysis of Reasoning LLM." The horizontal axis represents the number of shots, ranging from 0 to 4, while the vertical axis measures the token count, with values ranging from 0 to 7000. Each category on the x-axis contains two stacked bars: an orange bar representing "Reasoning" tokens and a blue bar representing "Demonstration" tokens. At zero shots, the reasoning token count is high at 6393, with no demonstration tokens. As the number of shots increases, the reasoning token count decreases significantly, dropping to 4500 at one shot, 4900 at two shots, 5200 at three shots, and 4600 at four shots. In contrast, demonstration tokens are introduced only in the one-shot, two-shot, three-shot, and four-shot scenarios, with values of 1952, 1613, 1040, and 1379, respectively. The chart highlights that few-shot prompting leads to a substantial reduction in reasoning tokens compared to zero-shot prompting, while also introducing demonstration tokens, which are absent in the zero-shot case. The error bars on top of each bar indicate variability in the token counts, with the largest error bars observed at zero shots and one shot.
